subject: Astronomy & Space
title: The Milky Way's Dark Matter Halo
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Milky Way's Dark Matter Halo.

hook.text: The visible Milky Way is just the tip. It's surrounded by a massive halo of invisible dark matter extending far beyond the stars.

buildup.text: The halo is roughly spherical and extends at least 300,000 light-years from the center—three times the disk's width.

discovery.text: Rotation curve measurements show the galaxy spins too fast for its visible mass. Dark matter provides the missing gravity.

twist.text: The dark matter halo contains about 10 times more mass than all the visible stars, gas, and dust combined.

climax.text: Dwarf galaxies orbit within the halo. Their paths help map the invisible matter that dominates our galaxy's mass.

punchline.text: Ten times more dark matter than visible stuff. We live inside an invisible cocoon.

quiz.question: How much more massive is the Milky Way's dark matter halo compared to visible matter?

details.summary: The Milky Way is embedded in a vast spherical halo of dark matter extending hundreds of thousands of light-years beyond the visible disk. This invisible halo contains 5-10 times more mass than all visible stars and gas combined.
details.whyItMatters: The dark matter halo determines the Milky Way's total mass and gravitational influence. Without it, the galaxy would fly apart. Understanding our own galaxy's halo is essential for dark matter research.
takeaways: A spherical dark matter halo extends far beyond the visible disk
Contains 5-10 times more mass than all visible matter
Keeps outer stars orbiting faster than visible mass explains

faq.question: How do we know the dark matter halo exists?
faq.answer: Stars and gas in the outer Milky Way orbit too fast for the visible mass to hold them. This flat rotation curve implies enormous unseen mass. Satellite galaxies orbiting the Milky Way, the motion of the Magellanic Clouds, and gravitational lensing studies all independently confirm the dark matter…

faq.question: How massive is the Milky Way's dark matter halo?
faq.answer: Total estimates range from about 1-2 trillion solar masses, depending on the method. The visible components (stars, gas, dust) account for about 100-200 billion solar masses.
